documents.title: In-app browser
documents.description: The in-app browser gives you and Codex a shared view of rendered web pages inside a thread. Use it when you're building or debugging a web app and want to preview pages and attach visual comments.
documents.summary: This document explains how to utilize the built-in browser and browser plugin within the Codex development environment to preview web applications, perform visual debugging, and provide feedback to the AI.

documents.title: Computer Use
documents.description: In the Codex app, computer use is currently available on macOS, except in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, and Switzerland at launch. Install the Computer Use plugin, then grant Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions when macOS prompts you.
documents.summary: This document explains how to set up, authorize, and safely utilize the computer use feature in the Codex app to interact with graphical user interfaces on macOS.

documents.title: Codex app features
documents.description: The Codex app is a focused desktop experience for working on Codex threads in parallel, with built-in worktree support, automations, and Git functionality.
documents.summary: This document provides an overview of the key features and capabilities of the Codex desktop application, including project management, Git integration, automation tools, and environment configurations.

documents.title: Review
documents.description: The review pane helps you understand what Codex changed, give targeted feedback, and decide what to keep.
documents.summary: This document explains how to use the Codex review pane to manage, inspect, and provide feedback on code changes within a Git repository. It covers navigation, inline commenting, pull request workflows, and Git staging operations.

documents.title: Worktrees
documents.description: In the Codex app, worktrees let Codex run multiple independent tasks in the same project without interfering with each other. documents.summary: This document details the authentication methods, security configurations, and credential management options available for accessing Codex tools and services.

documents.title: Codex CLI features
documents.description: Codex supports workflows beyond chat. Use this guide to learn what each one unlocks and when to use it.
documents.summary: This guide details the core functionality and workflows of the Codex CLI, covering interactive terminal sessions, session management, remote connectivity, model selection, and feature configuration.

documents.title: Slash commands in Codex CLI
documents.description: Slash commands give you fast, keyboard-first control over Codex. Type `/` in the composer to open the slash popup, choose a command, and Codex will perform actions such as switching models, adjusting permissions, or summarizing long conversations without leaving the terminal.
documents.summary: This document provides an overview of the slash commands available in the Codex CLI, detailing how to use them for session management, configuration, and workflow automation.

documents.title: Codex CLI
documents.description: Codex CLI is OpenAI's coding agent that you can run locally from your terminal. It can read, change, and run code on your machine in the selected directory. It's [open source](https://github.com/openai/codex) and built in Rust for speed and efficiency.
documents.summary: This document provides an overview and setup instructions for the Codex CLI, a terminal-based agent that allows developers to manage code, execute tasks, and interact with AI models directly from their environment.

documents.title: Codex web
documents.description: Codex is OpenAI's coding agent that can read, edit, and run code. It helps you build faster, fix bugs, and understand unfamiliar code. With Codex cloud, Codex can work on tasks in the background (including in parallel) using its own cloud environment.
documents.summary: This document provides an overview and setup guide for Codex, an AI coding agent designed to automate tasks, manage cloud environments, and integrate with GitHub workflows.

documents.title: Custom Prompts
documents.description: Custom prompts are deprecated. Use [skills](https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills) for reusable instructions that Codex can invoke explicitly or implicitly.
documents.summary: This document explains how to create and manage custom prompts for the Codex CLI and IDE extension using Markdown files and placeholder variables, while noting that the feature is deprecated in favor of skills.

documents.title: Managed configuration
documents.description: Enterprise admins can control local Codex behavior in two ways:
documents.summary: This document describes how enterprise administrators can enforce security requirements and managed defaults for Codex behavior across local and cloud environments.

documents.title: Codex GitHub Action
documents.description: Use the Codex GitHub Action (`openai/codex-action@v1`) to run Codex in CI/CD jobs, apply patches, or post reviews from a GitHub Actions workflow. The action installs the Codex CLI, starts the Responses API proxy when you provide an API key, and runs `codex exec` under the permissions you specify.
documents.summary: This document describes how to implement the Codex GitHub Action to automate code reviews, migration tasks, and quality checks within CI/CD pipelines.

documents.title: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md
documents.description: Codex reads `AGENTS.md` files before doing any work. By layering global guidance with project-specific overrides, you can start each task with consistent expectations, no matter which repository you open.
documents.summary: This document explains how to configure and structure AGENTS.md files to provide Codex with global and project-specific instructions. It details the discovery, precedence, and inheritance rules used to manage persistent behavioral guidance.

documents.title: Use Codex with the Agents SDK
documents.description: You can run Codex as an MCP server and connect it from other MCP clients (for example, an agent built with the [OpenAI Agents SDK MCP integration](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/integrations-observability#mcp)).
documents.summary: This guide explains how to run the Codex CLI as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and integrate it with the OpenAI Agents SDK to build automated, multi-agent workflows.

documents.title: Codex IDE extension features
documents.description: The Codex IDE extension gives you access to Codex directly in VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and other VS Code-compatible editors. It uses the same agent as the Codex CLI and shares the same configuration.
documents.summary: This document provides an overview of the features and functionality available in the Codex IDE extension, including model selection, agent settings, cloud task management, and integrated AI tools.

documents.title: Codex IDE extension
documents.description: Codex is OpenAI's coding agent that can read, edit, and run code. It helps you build faster, squash bugs, and understand unfamiliar code. With the Codex VS Code extension, you can use Codex side by side in your IDE or delegate tasks to Codex Cloud.
documents.summary: This document provides installation, configuration, and setup instructions for the Codex IDE extension across various coding environments like VS Code and JetBrains.

documents.title: Use Codex in GitHub
documents.description: Use Codex to review pull requests without leaving GitHub. Add a pull request comment with `@codex review`, and Codex replies with a standard GitHub code review.
documents.summary: This document provides instructions on how to integrate and configure Codex for automated code reviews and task management within GitHub pull requests.

documents.title: Use Codex in Linear
documents.description: Use Codex in Linear to delegate work from issues. Assign an issue to Codex or mention `@Codex` in a comment, and Codex creates a cloud task and replies with progress and results.
documents.summary: This document provides instructions for integrating and using Codex within Linear to delegate project management tasks and automate issue resolution. It covers setup procedures, delegation methods, automation through triage rules, and configuration for local development environments.

documents.title: Use Codex in Slack
documents.description: Use Codex in Slack to kick off coding tasks from channels and threads. Mention `@Codex` with a prompt, and Codex creates a cloud task and replies with the results.
documents.summary: This document provides instructions for integrating and using the Codex Slack application to initiate coding tasks directly from Slack channels and threads.

documents.description: Chronicle is in an **opt-in research preview**. It is only available for ChatGPT Pro subscribers on macOS, and is not yet available in the EU, UK and Switzerland. documents.summary: Chronicle is a feature that augments Codex memories by capturing screen context to provide relevant information and reduce the need for manual prompt context. This document outlines the setup, privacy considerations, operational controls, and security risks associated with the tool.

documents.description: Non-interactive mode lets you run Codex from scripts (for example, continuous integration (CI) jobs) without opening the interactive TUI. You invoke it with `codex exec`.

documents.title: Sandbox
documents.description: The sandbox is the boundary that lets Codex act autonomously without giving it unrestricted access to your machine. When Codex runs local commands in the **Codex app**, **IDE extension**, or **CLI**, those commands run inside a constrained environment instead of running with full access by default.
documents.summary: This document explains the purpose and configuration of the Codex sandbox, a security feature that provides a constrained environment for agentic tasks to execute commands safely.

It covers core terminology, best practices for triggering parallel workflows, and guidelines for selecting appropriate models and reasoning efforts.

documents.title: Agent internet access
documents.description: By default, Codex blocks internet access during the agent phase. Setup scripts still run with internet access so you can install dependencies. You can enable agent internet access per environment when you need it.

documents.title: Config basics
documents.description: Codex reads configuration details from more than one location. Your personal defaults live in `~/.codex/config.toml`, and you can add project overrides with `.codex/config.toml` files. For security, Codex loads project `.codex/` layers only when you trust the project.
documents.summary: This document explains how to configure Codex using TOML files, detailing the file locations, configuration precedence hierarchy, and common settings available for customization.

documents.title: Sample Configuration
documents.description: Use this example configuration as a starting point. It includes most keys Codex reads from `config.toml`, along with default behaviors, recommended values where helpful, and short notes.

documents.title: Model Context Protocol
documents.description: Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects models to tools and context. Use it to give Codex access to third-party documentation, or to let it interact with developer tools like your browser or Figma.

documents.title: Memories
documents.description: Memories are off by default and aren't available in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or Switzerland at launch. Enable them in Codex settings, or set `memories = true` in the `[features]` table in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
documents.summary: This document explains how to enable, configure, and manage the Memories feature in Codex, which allows the assistant to maintain context across multiple user sessions.

documents.title: Remote connections
documents.description: SSH remote connections are currently in alpha. To enable them today, set `remote_connections = true` in the `[features]` table in `~/.codex/config.toml`. Availability, setup flows, and supported environments may change as the feature improves.
documents.summary: This document outlines how to enable and configure SSH-based remote connections in the Codex application to access projects hosted on external machines.
